body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/37983

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/831

## What changed

- Forward `window_size` and `s_aux` from `VisionTritonAttention` into the Triton varlen prefill kernel.
- Apply left/right local-window bounds while preserving causal and packed-sequence masks.
- Model each per-query-head attention sink as a value-less virtual softmax logit by seeding the online-softmax state.
- Guard fully masked KV blocks so narrow and one-sided windows do not introduce NaNs.
- Validate sink shape, contiguity, and device.
- Add a failing-before/passing-after backend regression and independent numerical boundary coverage.

This overlaps the still-open upstream candidate https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38142. I inspected that work and the earlier experimental commit linked from the issue before applying the narrow kernel/backend correction here.

## Reproduction and validation

On the recorded base, this failed because `VisionTritonAttention` silently dropped the two kwargs, while the legacy full-attention calibration passed:

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-956e818f217c/venv/bin/python /tmp/test_triton_attention_window_sink.py \
  TestTritonAttentionWindowSink.test_reference_matches_hand_computed_example \
  TestTritonAttentionWindowSink.test_kernel_matches_reference_full_attention \
  TestTritonAttentionWindowSink.test_backend_window_and_sinks_acceptance
```

After the change:

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-956e818f217c/venv/bin/python \
  test/registered/kernel/attention/test_triton_attention_window_sink.py
# Ran 14 tests: OK (13 passed, Hopper-only FA3 cross-check skipped)

/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-956e818f217c/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_vision_max_seqlen.py
# 7 passed

pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/prefill_attention.py \
  python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py \
  test/registered/kernel/attention/test_triton_attention_window_sink.py
# passed
```

The numerical suite ran on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (`gfx950`, ROCm 7.2) and compares BF16 kernel output against an independent FP32 PyTorch implementation. It covers the hand-computed anchor, window-only, sink-only, combined semantics, ragged batches, GQA, causal composition, one-sided/tiny windows spanning multiple KV blocks, NaN resistance, backend forwarding, and invalid sink shape.

## Limitations

- MiMo-V2.5 weights were unavailable, so this does not claim a full-model serving or semantic-output reproduction.
- The assigned hardware was AMD gfx950, not the NVIDIA B40/H20 in the report.
- The FA3 parity test requires NVIDIA Hopper and was skipped on this host.
- No native C++ or FlyDSL component changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.

Structured results and raw logs are under `reports/j-956e818f217c/`.
